media.altText: Detail of a 1955 magazine photograph showing Franz Waxman in glasses, playing a saxophone.
media.description: The printed caption identifies the two men by what they are holding rather than by position: "FRANZ WAXMAN (with saxophone), music director and conductor of the 1955 Los Angeles Music Festival, rehearses with Les Brown for the opening night concert of the Festival on June 6. Waxman conducted Brown's Band of Renown and the Festival Symphony Orchestra in the West Coast premiere of Liebermann's Concerto for Jazz Band and Symphony Orchestra." The archive reproduces the man with the saxophone. The photograph carries the credit "Photo: Dave Pell."
media.publicCaption: Franz Waxman, who appears in this archive with Trouble for Two (1936), A Day at the Races (1937) and The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1939). The photograph is much later: he was rehearsing with Les Brown's Band of Renown for the opening concert of the Los Angeles Music Festival in June 1955, which he conducted.
media.publicCreditLine: Photograph credited to Dave Pell; Musical Courier, vol. 152, no. 1 (July 1955), p. 27; Summy-Birchard Publishing Company; scanned copy at the Internet Archive.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The photograph was published in a United States periodical in July 1955, so its copyright would have had to be renewed in 1982 or 1983 to survive; that renewal has not been checked, which leaves the status unverified rather than known to be free. The photograph also carries a separate photographer's credit. The scan is openly viewable at the Internet Archive, but open access is not a licence. A reduced-resolution detail (340 × 490 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper colleague.
